question: A 3×4 real matrix has rank 2. Find the dimension of its right null space.

solution.asked: Find nullity of A acting on R⁴.
steps: The input space has dimension equal to the number of columns, 4.
Rank accounts for 2 independent image directions.
Nullity is 4−2=2.
commonMistakes: Right-null-space dimension uses columns; the left null space uses rows.

hints: Identify the conditions under which rank–nullity theorem applies.
Start from $ \dim\ker A=n-\operatorname{rank}A $.

verification.method: Construct rank-2 3×4 representative and verify rank/nullity dimensions. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: Which statements about causal discrete-time LTI systems with rational H(z) and no pole-zero cancellations are true?

options.text: All poles strictly inside the unit circle imply BIBO stability
A pole at z=1 is strictly BIBO stable
The causal ROC lies outside the outermost pole
All numerator zeros must lie inside the unit circle for BIBO stability

solution.asked: Select valid causal ROC and stability conditions.
steps: A causal ROC extends outward from the largest pole magnitude.
It contains the unit circle exactly when every pole is strictly inside that circle.
A boundary pole is not strictly stable; numerator zeros do not impose the claimed BIBO condition. Select A and C.

hints: Identify the conditions under which discrete-time pole stability applies.

question: For a differentiable real function on an open interval, which statements are valid?

options.text: An interior local extremum has derivative zero
A zero derivative at one point guarantees a local maximum
Every stationary point is a local minimum
A stationary point can be neither a maximum nor a minimum

solution.asked: Select necessary and non-sufficient extremum facts.
steps: Fermat’s theorem gives derivative zero at a differentiable interior extremum.
The converse fails: x³ has derivative zero at 0 but is increasing through that point.
Thus stationary points can be inflections rather than extrema; select A and D.
solution.explanation: Thus stationary points can be inflections rather than extrema; select A and D.
commonMistakes: Necessary conditions for an extremum are not sufficient conditions.

hints: Identify the conditions under which stationary-point logic applies.
Start from $ \text{interior extremum}\Rightarrow f\prime(c)=0 $.

verification.method: Fermat interior-extremum theorem with x³ stationary nonextremum counterexample. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

steps: Cancel the explicit integrator factor before taking the limit.

The closed-loop denominator s²+2s+10 has negative-real-part poles, consistent with the stated stability.
